import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ringel's Conjecture

*Reference:* G. Ringel, *Problem 25*, in *Theory of Graphs and its Applications*
(Proc. Sympos. Smolenice, 1963), Academia, Prague, 1964.

Ringel's conjecture (1963): the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into copies of any tree
with $n$ edges. It remains open; the case of all sufficiently large $n$ is proved by
Montgomery–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov, see `Arxiv/2001.02665/RingelConjecture.lean`.
-/
namespace RingelConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/--
For any tree $T$ with $n$ edges, the complete graph $K_{2n+1}$ decomposes into
$2n+1$ edge-disjoint copies of $T$.

A "copy" of $T$ is the image $T.\text{map}(f_i)$ of $T$ under a vertex embedding
$f_i : V \hookrightarrow \text{Fin}(2n+1)$; the copies are pairwise edge-disjoint
and together cover every edge of $K_{2n+1}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem ringel_conjecture {V : Type} [Finite V]
    (T : SimpleGraph V) (hT : T.IsTree)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : T.edgeSet.ncard = n) :
    ∃ f : Fin (2 * n + 1) → (V ↪ Fin (2 * n + 1)),
      Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (T.map (f i)).edgeSet (T.map (f j)).edgeSet) ∧
      ⨆ i, T.map (f i) = (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2 * n + 1))) := by
  sorry

end RingelConjecture

reformulations.difference: The source describes a decomposition into edge-disjoint subgraphs isomorphic to T. Lean represents copies using injective vertex maps and expresses coverage by a graph supremum equal to ⊤. Each mapped graph retains unused host vertices as isolated vertices.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For an injection f, (T.map f).edgeSet is exactly the image of T.edgeSet under the induced injection on unordered pairs. Restricting T.map f to range f gives a graph isomorphic to T; the additional isolated host vertices contribute no edges. Conversely, an isomorphism onto an ordinary copy supplies such a vertex injection. The scratch file constructs the range isomorphism and proves that the Lean conclusion is equivalent to the existence of an embedding family in which every pair of distinct host vertices is adjacent in exactly one image. Thus the disjointness and supremum conditions express precisely the required edge decomposition.

review.notes: Reviewed the file's sole theorem. IsTree excludes empty vertex types, and [Finite V] prevents edgeSet.ncard from taking its infinite-set default value. Independently proved that a tree with n edges has n+1 vertices and that the conclusion holds for every zero-edge tree. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles successfully, verifies concrete n=1 and n=2 decompositions, and proves that the hypotheses are satisfiable for every n. The equivalence and zero-case proofs have no sorryAx dependency. The original proceedings text was inaccessible; the mathematical claim was checked against its explicit restatement in Montgomery–Pokrovskiy–Sudakov. Their theorem is restricted to sufficiently large n, consistent with the all-n declaration's research open status.
